steps.title: Apply online for your study permit (your eTA comes with the approval)
steps.why: You need a study permit to study in Canada, and as a citizen of a visa-exempt country you also need an electronic travel authorization (eTA) to fly to Canada. IRCC issues the eTA together with your study permit approval — you don't need to apply separately or pay another fee. Once approved, you'll receive a port of entry letter of introduction (not the permit itself) that includes your eTA information; you show it to a border services officer on arrival and receive your study permit at the port of entry. Your eTA is linked to your passport and is valid for 5 years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first, so you must travel on the same passport you used to apply.
prerequisites: Valid letter of acceptance from UBC
Valid passport (travel with this same passport — your eTA will be linked to it)
An IRCC secure account to pay fees, submit your application and check status
A scanner or camera to make electronic copies of your documents
A valid credit or debit card (Canadian bank INTERAC® Online registered for online banking, or any Visa Debit card; the card does not have to be in your name)
Your local visa office instructions for the country/territory you're applying from
The instruction guide, read before completing the forms
Answers prepared for the online tool's questions, which generate your personalized document checklist
steps.cost: Study permit application fees are paid in your IRCC account by credit or debit card; no separate application or additional fee is required for the eTA.

steps.title: Book and give your biometrics within 30 days of the IRCC letter
steps.why: IRCC collects biometrics (fingerprints and photo) for most study permit applications to confirm your identity and help assess your application. After you apply, you'll get a biometrics instruction letter — you have 30 days to give your biometrics, and booking your collection appointment as soon as you can avoids processing delays. Biometrics are valid for 10 years, making repeat trips to Canada easier.
prerequisites: Submitted study permit application online (with letter of acceptance and PAL/TAL)
Paid the biometrics fee at the time you submitted your application
Received the biometrics instruction letter from IRCC
steps.cost: CAN$85 per applicant; maximum CAN$170 for families applying at the same time (spouse/common-law partner and dependent children)
steps.time_estimate: Must be completed within 30 days of receiving the IRCC biometrics letter

steps.title: Book and complete your immigration medical exam with an IRCC panel physician
steps.why: Only a physician authorized by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (a "panel physician") can perform an immigration medical exam — you cannot use your own family doctor unless their name appears on IRCC's panel physician list. You must also be in good health to be admitted to Canada when you arrive with your study permit approval, so completing the exam with the right doctor keeps your study permit application moving.
prerequisites: Your study permit application details, including where your application is being processed (you must tell the panel physician so results are sent to the correct office)
A valid travel document, such as your passport
The IRCC list of panel physicians to find an authorized doctor in your area — you may choose a panel physician anywhere in the world
A means of payment: you are responsible for the cost of the exam
steps.cost: Paid by you; the fee varies from one panel physician to another
steps.time_estimate: Book as early as possible before you travel — results are sent by the physician to the visa office processing your application

steps.title: Pay your Term 1 tuition from abroad before the September 9, 2026 deadline
steps.why: Your Term 1 Winter Session tuition — covering Term 1 courses, the first half of two-term courses, and most student fees — is due September 9, 2026. Because you are paying from outside Canada, start the transfer early enough that funds clear by the deadline; an international bank wire in a major currency corridor is generally straightforward but still needs a few business days to settle. Your exact assessed amount appears under "Finances" in Workday once fees are assessed, so check there rather than relying on estimates.
prerequisites: Accepted your offer and paid the acceptance deposit through the Applicant Service Centre ($3,000 for students on a study permit)
Registered for your Winter Session courses so your fees are assessed
Checked the assessed amount under "Finances" in Workday
Reviewed the UBC Vancouver or UBC Okanagan Calendar and the cost estimator to anticipate the total
Confirmed your bank's international transfer limits, fees, and processing time, and gathered standard proof-of-funds documentation
steps.cost: Term 1 tuition and most student fees as assessed in Workday (use the UBC cost estimator for a projection); plus the temporary iMED international student insurance fee of $237 (or $338 for one-term exchange students) plus a $10.54 direct billing fee, charged to your account when you register
steps.time_estimate: 1–2 hours to set up the transfer, plus several business days for funds to arrive — initiate well before September 9, 2026

steps.title: Prepare your port of entry documents for arrival in Canada
steps.why: Your study permit isn't issued until you land — a border services officer reviews your documents and prints your permit at the port of entry. The letter of introduction is not your study permit, and if you have an eTA there's no sticker in your passport (it's linked electronically to the passport you applied with), so arriving with the wrong passport or without your letter can delay or prevent entry.
prerequisites: Study permit application approved by IRCC
Port of entry letter of introduction received from the visa office
Valid letter of acceptance from your UBC (designated learning institution)
steps.time_estimate: 1–2 hours to gather documents; keep them in your carry-on

applies_to_rules: Carry a valid travel document, such as the passport you used to apply for your study permit — if you have an eTA, it is linked to that passport and is valid for 5 years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first

steps.title: Apply for your Social Insurance Number (SIN) with Service Canada
steps.why: A SIN is the 9-digit number you need to work in Canada, open most types of bank accounts, and access government programs and benefits — so you can't be paid for on-campus or off-campus work without one. As a temporary resident, your SIN starts with "9" and expires with your immigration documents, so note the expiry and reapply to extend it before it lapses. Apply online for faster processing, and protect your SIN as soon as it is issued — it is private and illegal for anyone else to use.
prerequisites: Be 12 years or older (anyone 12+ can apply for their own SIN)
One primary identity document proving your legal status in Canada (e.g. your immigration document)
One secondary identity document confirming your identity
Supporting documents if your name has changed, plus translations if a document is not in English or French
Check that all details are correct before applying — if there is an error on a document, contact the issuing source to fix it first
applies_to_rules: Temporary residents (study permit holders): SIN begins with "9" and expires with your immigration documents; apply again to extend the expiry date
If you already know your SIN, do not reapply — view and print it by signing in to My Service Canada Account (MSCA)
Service Canada no longer issues plastic SIN cards; if yours is lost or damaged, request a Confirmation of SIN letter
If Service Canada cannot issue you a SIN, you may request a temporary tax number (TTN) from the CRA by filing your return or benefit application with a letter explaining why you have no SIN
If you make a mistake or forget a document, you cannot edit your application — submit a new one with all required documents again

steps.title: Enrol in BC's Medical Services Plan (MSP) after you arrive
steps.why: All B.C. residents must enrol in MSP, and UBC notes that if you don't have other medical coverage you are required by B.C. law to register. Coverage only starts three months after your arrival date in B.C. \u2014 if you arrive in August, your waiting period will likely end in November \u2014 so applying as soon as you arrive keeps that gap as short as possible. During the wait period you need private coverage: as a UBC international student, the temporary iMED insurance fee is charged to your account when you register for courses and covers you until MSP begins (likely in November). Note that coverage depends on residency: if you leave B.C. within 6 months of enrolling, you may have to repay your medical expenses.
prerequisites: Arrival in British Columbia (the 3-month wait period is counted from your arrival date)
Course registration at UBC, which triggers the temporary iMED insurance charge to your student account
Apply online \u2014 the easiest and fastest way to enrol; completing MSP enrolment and receiving your Personal Health Number (PHN) is tied to the B.C. Services Card
steps.cost: MSP: $0 for Canadian citizens and permanent residents; $75/month for students on a study permit. Temporary iMED insurance: $237 (or $338 for one-term exchange students), plus a $10.54 direct billing fee.
steps.time_estimate: Apply as soon as you arrive; coverage begins about 3 months later (from November 1, 2026 onward if you arrived in August)

steps.title: Check your MSP application status and plan for the 3-month wait period
steps.why: MSP enrolment isn't instant — as a new resident your coverage only starts after a wait period of the balance of the month you established residence in B.C. plus two months (roughly three months after your arrival date). Following up confirms your application was received and that you'll get your Personal Health Number and B.C. Services Card, and it reminds you to hold private health insurance for the entire gap. Note also that if you leave B.C. within 6 months of enrolling, you may have to repay your medical expenses.
prerequisites: MSP application for enrolment already submitted (online, in person or by mail)
Arrival date in B.C. on hand to calculate your wait period end date
Private health insurance in place to cover you until MSP starts (or, if you moved from another province, continued coverage from your former provincial plan)
If your coverage will be under an employer, union or pension group plan, your group administrator's contact details
steps.cost: No cost to apply for or enrol in MSP
steps.time_estimate: 15–30 minutes to follow up; coverage begins after the wait period (balance of arrival month plus two months)
